tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

schema.name: SendFeedback
schema.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	# Notes for issue #230: a web control surface on the remote port
2	
3	Read: CLAUDE.md, docs/design.md (Trust boundary, Remote client 2026-10-12 and its status entries), docs/lessons.md, docs/remote-client.md in full. Line numbers below are from this worktree (branch `dispatch/230-...`, at "Release 0.4.1"). Nothing was run: no build, no test, no browser.
4	
5	## 1. On-disk record and rehydration (before any pane)
6	
7	Workspaces are data, processes are a cache. The web surface adds almost no new durable data, and the notes say where the tree currently has none.
8	
9	- **Already durable, and enough for a browser device.** `devices.json` (`PairedDevice` in `src/ports/remote.rs`: id, name, scope, `token_sha256`, created, last_seen) and `identity.json` (`Identity`: server_id, name, certificate, `spki_sha256`, listen). A browser is one more `PairedDevice`. Revocation is `AppAction::RevokeDevice` (`src/core/remote.rs:86`) deleting the row. That is the whole server-side record. No schema bump is needed unless a field is added to `PairedDevice` (e.g. a device "kind" or user-agent string). `#[serde(default)]` would make that additive, but `identity.json`/`devices.json` have their own versioning (`IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION`), not `SCHEMA_VERSION`. [tree] to confirm whether a `devices.json` change needs a migration step.
10	- **No tombstone for a revoked device.** A revoked token and a never-known token are the same thing to the host: `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) answers 401 `unauthorized`, "the token is not known; pair again". The acceptance line "revoke the phone and the page says so on its next request" cannot be met from the current reply. It would need either a tombstone (hash of revoked tokens, a new durable record) or the page saying "not paired or revoked" for both. The issue asks for "revoked" and "identity changed" to be said plainly, so this is a decision.
11	- **The page's own state (client side), rehydrated per load:** the token (a cookie or `localStorage`, decision 2), the pinned `spki_sha256` and `server_id` from the pairing URL, the last revision. Everything else (sessions, conversation, screen) is in memory and refetched, as the Swift client does (§7 "What the client keeps": nothing from a host on disk). Rehydration of a page = load HTML, read the stored credential, `GET /api/v1/info`, open `/api/v1/events`, wait for `hello`, fetch snapshots, apply buffered events by revision (§4.4 "Subscribe first, then snapshot"). The existing protocol already gives that; the page re-implements the Swift client's reconcile (per-key held revision, epoch change refetches everything, `resync_required` reconnects).
12	- **The pairing window** is not saved (`PairingWindow` in core, `OpenPairing` at `src/core/remote.rs:46`; code made by `remote::pairing_code()`, 40 bits, single use, three failures close it). A URL carrying the code is therefore valid only while that in-memory window is open.

59	## 3. Findings that bear on the decisions
60	
61	1. **What a self-signed click-through buys is narrower than the issue's framing, and the `key` check has nothing to compare against in the browser.** Page JS cannot read the TLS certificate or its SPKI. The only "key presented by `/info`" available to the page is the `spki_sha256` field of the `/info` JSON, which is whatever the answering server writes. A page served by the impostor serves its own page and its own `/info`. So the URL's `key` guards against reaching the wrong genuine Switchboard by address (a reused DHCP address, two Macs), not against an attacker. On the host side, `remote_pair` (`:3606`) already refuses a `/pair` whose body key is not the host's own, and the page would put the URL's key in that body: against a genuine host that is the only meaningful check; against an impostor the impostor decides. That is the same as the issue's own statement; the notes add that the comparison is page-side and unenforceable from the host's point of view.
62	2. **Cookies are not port-scoped.** A cookie set by `https://192.168.1.5:43187` is sent to every other port on that host, and a `__Host-` prefix constrains Domain/Path/Secure but not port. Two Switchboard instances on one machine (the dev aid `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT`, and tests use it) would share a cookie name unless it carries the server id. `SameSite=Strict` is about site, not origin, so another page on a different port of the same IP is same-site: CSRF on `POST /send` and cross-site-WebSocket-hijack protections need an explicit check (Origin or Host, or a custom request header), none of which exists, because the port has only ever had bearer headers, which a cross-origin page cannot attach. Moving to ambient credentials (a cookie) removes that property for the whole `/api/v1` surface, including the native clients' routes: the cookie is accepted at the same endpoints. This is the largest security consequence of decision 2 and should be named in the plan.
63	3. **The unauthenticated pool is 4 and a browser's page load is bursty.** HTML, CSS, JS, favicon, `/info`, each possibly on its own TLS connection (browsers open up to ~6 per host), all unauthenticated until a reply with `authenticated: true`. A page load by a stranger-or-owner can occupy the pool, and the pool does not distinguish a browser from a flood. Static replies are also not rate-limited. If the page is served on the frame, it competes with the 8-per-pass drain and the 64 inbox; if served on the connection thread, that skips the frame (and the rule "handlers are thin; no logic in the adapter") but needs a pool decision. A paired browser also holds a paired slot per WebSocket for as long as the tab lives, out of 12 shared with the headset and the CLI.
64	4. **The pairing code lands in the host's request line.** A URL `GET /?code=...` is read by `read_request` into `RemoteRequest.query` (`:496-505`), so the code crosses the TLS connection and sits in the frame's memory like any query. It is not logged by `refuse` (path only). Also: the browser's history entry exists until `replaceState` runs, a `Referer` carries the URL to any subresource that is not same-origin (there should be none under the CSP the issue asks for), and some browsers sync history or open links from a camera app in a different process before the page script runs. A fragment (`#code=`) never reaches the host or a Referer and `replaceState` still works on it; the issue chose the query string. Whether that is deliberate is a question, not a finding.
65	5. **The code is single use, the URL is a bearer of it.** Anyone who can see the QR for the five-minute window (a screen share, a photo of the dialog) has the code; the key in the QR does not authenticate the person, as today with the JSON QR. No change from the native flow, but the URL is now also in the phone's camera/Messages/clipboard apps. Equivalent to "Copy invite".
66	6. **Cert has no SAN.** Even with the click-through, some browsers apply extra rules to certificates they treat as untrusted (HSTS-like blocks, no "Proceed" on some versions for no-SAN, ATS-like policies on iOS WebKit for `WebSocket`/`fetch`). Whether a no-SAN, IP-literal, self-signed P-256 certificate can be click-through-accepted on iOS Safari and Android Chrome, and whether that acceptance extends to `wss://` and to `fetch` is what decides option A (click-through) versus option B (host offers its certificate). Not checked.
67	7. **The spec's sentences to amend** (the plan is told to amend the spec and the status section): `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1 (bounds: "a TLS handshake..."; the pools; add the page's place in them), §4.3 (add the static paths, which are outside the `/api/v1` allowlist and not in the table; "Everything else on the wire is refused before translation" holds for `/api/v1` only), §5 (line 306 "Require pairing before anything but /info and /pair"; line 309 the QR payload JSON, "scans or types both"; line 312 "It is sent only as a bearer header ... never in a URL", which a cookie contradicts; line 313 "The client stores the token and the pinned key hash in its Keychain"; line 317 "The client verifies the pin on every connection" which a browser cannot), and the design.md sections "Remote client (2026-10-12)" (A1 sentence on "everything else is refused by name", "the QR carrying the server id, key hash, code and address") and "Known gaps". README (Layout row for `web/`, `src/adapters/remote.rs`, `src/ui/remote.rs`, `tests/remote.rs`; dev aids; the `pbpaste` pairing line at ~276), CHANGELOG Unreleased line, and the dialog's text.
68	8. **Static assets and the layering rule.** The page files are data embedded with `include_str!` (no precedent for text assets in `src`, only `include_bytes!` for fonts and the icon in `src/main.rs:167`, `src/ui/theme.rs:203`). A `web/` directory at the repo root would also need `Cargo.toml` `include`/`exclude` and the bundle script checks (`scripts/bundle.sh`) [tree] not read. CLAUDE.md: `src/core` is deterministic and `src/ui` only draws; the page is neither, it is adapter data. Where the path table lives (adapter or `app.rs`) is a design call; `serve_remote` is where the allowlist lives today.
69	9. **Hard rules touched.** No keystroke injection: not relevant to the page's own JS. Never write into a project's `.claude/`/`.switchboard/`: not touched. Secret values: the page shows redacted text only; the page's CSP and storage choice are what keep a token out of script reach. No client names anywhere that reaches GitHub: nothing in this issue needs one. Attribution: CLAUDE.md forbids a `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with" line in commits and PR bodies, overriding the harness reminder; the plan's commit and PR steps should say so.

A secure-context question for `crypto`, service workers and cookies `Secure`, too: does a page on a click-through origin count as a secure context in each browser?

A spike (`spikes/…`) is what CLAUDE.md calls for before building on a risky mechanism; none exists for browsers.

106	- [owner] Option A (the click-through on the local network is the trust step, said in the paired-devices dialog) or B (the host offers its certificate for download to trust on the device first): which, given what a phone can do with each. This is a call on taste and risk; the tree cannot settle it, and part of it needs a device.

138	
139	Throwaway crates and scripts that answered the Spike 0 questions in
140	`docs/design.md` before any product code was written. Each directory has a
141	README with the commands run, their output, and a recommendation. They are
142	kept for reference and are not built by the main crate.
143	
144	| Dir | Question | Answer |
145	| --- | --- | --- |
146	| `01-claude-resume` | Can Claude Code sessions be captured and resumed? | Yes: `--session-id <uuid>` at launch, `--resume <uuid>` later from any terminal. Transcripts pruned after 30 days unless `cleanupPeriodDays` is raised. |
147	| `02-process-host` | tmux or own PTYs? | tmux on a private server: sessions outlive the app, reattach works, ~3 ms round trip. PTY adapter kept as fallback and for tests. |
148	| `03-session-state` | How to know "waiting on you"? | Claude Code hooks (`PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`) via a tiny `switchboard-hook` binary and a Unix socket; OSC 777 text from the raw stream as the hook-free fallback. |
149	| `05-keychain` | Can secrets live in the Keychain without prompts? | Yes for a bundle signed with a stable identity and identifier: the item ACL is `identifier + certificate`, so rebuilds read silently. Ad-hoc builds prompt per rebuild. |
150	| `06-pane-size` | Why is the embedded pane wider than the widget? | `window-size manual` ignored the client; `latest` makes the window follow whichever client attached last. Re-applied on launch for servers that outlive the app. |
151	| `07-clone-session` | Can a session be cloned up to a chosen message? | Yes: copy the transcript prefix before the chosen prompt, substitute a fresh UUID for `sessionId`, save it `0600` beside the original; `--resume <new>` opens the truncated history and the original is untouched. |
152	| `08-promptbox-embed` | Can Prompt Box be the agent message box? | Yes: same egui 0.36, drawn into a bottom panel unchanged, a `Clipboard` adapter turns Send into a hand-off; needs an embedded mode, a sink port, and focus-scoped shortcuts in promptbox. |
153	| `09-popout` | Can a session live in a window of its own? | Yes: an immediate viewport drawn from the main frame holds the page, terminal, and side panel; its frame is saved to settings and restored. |
154	| `10-nunchuk-serial` | Can a nunchuk drive the working set over USB serial? | Yes: one line per button change or stick flick from the Feather, read on a thread that reconnects; round trip 2 to 9 ms. Firmware in `firmware/nunchuk`. |
155	| `11-gate-sandbox` | Can Dispatch's pipeline commands be confined to the ticket's tree on macOS? | Yes: `sandbox-exec` with `(allow default)`, writes denied except the tree, the attempt directory, the lane's caches and a base set; ~5 ms start-up; a refused write is `EPERM` and a tagged `deny(1)` line in the unified log. `setuid` programs and keychain creation fail inside it. |
156	| `12-hidden-frames` | Does the frame loop keep running while the window is occluded or minimized? | Not before the fix: with the app hidden, a control query timed out after 10 s and was answered at once on unhide. With the tick and `pump` in `App::logic`, hidden queries answer in 75 to 103 ms (eframe's 100 ms throttle for invisible windows). The sleep and wake cycle is not yet measured. |
157	| `13-dispatch-service` | Can a Dispatch service be a Switchboard service session, and how is its port read? | Yes: `$SHELL -lc 'exec "$@"' dispatch-service env PORT=<port> npm start` finds `npm`, answers (CRA in 27 s), and is gone with its port 200 ms after `kill-session`. A port is free only if `0.0.0.0`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` all bind: CRA listens on `*`, which a loopback bind does not see. |
158	| `14-env-exec` | Do a pane's record id and launch token reach a child, so `switchboard-env exec` can resolve its sets? | Yes for a shell grandchild of a tmux pane started with `-e`; the binary's path is covered by `tests/control.rs`. The `aws-vault` form and the no-prompt run under Dispatch's launch flags were not run and are left to the owner. |
159	| `15-paste-buffer` | Can a multi-line send be bracketed only for a pane that asked for it? | Yes: `load-buffer -` then `paste-buffer -p -r -d` frames the text in `ESC[200~` .. `ESC[201~` for a pane with `bracket_paste_flag` 1 and delivers it bare otherwise; `-r` keeps LF, `-d` leaves no buffer. CR passes through and tmux 3.7c shows ESC as a literal `^[`, so the sender turns CR into LF and removes ESC. `send-keys -H` passes the markers to every pane. Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
160	| `16-base-pipeline` | Can Dispatch find a merged pull request's merge commit and read the base's pipeline on it? | GitHub, yes: `mergeCommit` on `gh pr list` and `gh pr view`, and the commit's `check-runs` (a short hash works) show the base's run in progress and then finished. Bitbucket's reads were not run (the token could not be read in the run); the adapter follows the documented `merge_commit.hash`, commit `statuses` and pipeline `steps`, with a read by number when a list row lacks the commit; until they are run, a wait on a Bitbucket base pipeline is refused. |
161	| `18-tmux-argv` | Do `new-session -e` values show in a process listing, and can they reach tmux another way? | Yes, they did: the server keeps the argv of the client that started it. `tmux start-server \; source-file -` with the `new-session` line on stdin keeps every value and the pane command off any argv; cold and warm both work, errors still return, and double-quoted values with `\n` for line breaks round-trip (single quotes lose a line starting with `#`). Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
162	| `19-structured-ask` | Does a card's answer to a structured ask reach interactive Claude Code as the next user message, sent once, both at the prompt and when held until the turn's `Stop`? | Yes: `Owner answered "<question>": <answer>`, typed as one line, arrived as its own user message once in both cases; a held answer went out only after the `Stop`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.293 by the ignored gate test `a_structured_answer_arrives_as_the_next_prompt`. |
163	| `21-evidence-writes` | Which writes reach a stage's evidence directory, outside the agent's cwd, without a prompt? | The Write tool, under the attempt directory's `Edit(//<dir>/**)` rule. Bash `cp`, `mv` and `mkdir` ask, and `--add-dir` does not change that. A Playwright MCP screenshot is refused outside the server's roots unless it runs with `--allow-unrestricted-file-access`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.295 and `@playwright/mcp@0.0.82`. |
164	| `22-remote-port` | Can a pinned-TLS HTTP and WebSocket port run on std with every request answered by the frame thread, and what does it cost? | Yes: `rustls` + `rcgen` + `tungstenite` + `mdns-sd`, no Tokio; the frame's share is under 0.25 ms per pass, latency is one frame interval, the pools and the subscriber overflow hold under a stall and an unread socket, Bonjour is seen by `dns-sd`. A 146 MB transcript parses in 290 ms at 575 MB peak, so content work leaves the frame thread. ctime and inode see the file changes mtime and size miss. |
165	| `04-terminal-view` | Embedded terminal or hand-off? | Hand off agents to Ghostty (`open -na Ghostty --args ... -e cmd`, raise by title); embed `egui_term` for shells, commands, services. |
166	
167	Findings are folded into `docs/design.md` under "Spike 0 results".

# Notes for issue #230: a web control surface on the remote port

Read: CLAUDE.md, docs/design.md (Trust boundary, Remote client 2026-10-12 and its status entries), docs/lessons.md, docs/remote-client.md in full. Line numbers below are from this worktree (branch `dispatch/230-...`, at "Release 0.4.1"). Nothing was run: no build, no test, no browser.

## 1. On-disk record and rehydration (before any pane)

Workspaces are data, processes are a cache. The web surface adds almost no new durable data, and the notes say where the tree currently has none.

- **Already durable, and enough for a browser device.** `devices.json` (`PairedDevice` in `src/ports/remote.rs`: id, name, scope, `token_sha256`, created, last_seen) and `identity.json` (`Identity`: server_id, name, certificate, `spki_sha256`, listen). A browser is one more `PairedDevice`. Revocation is `AppAction::RevokeDevice` (`src/core/remote.rs:86`) deleting the row. That is the whole server-side record. No schema bump is needed unless a field is added to `PairedDevice` (e.g. a device "kind" or user-agent string). `#[serde(default)]` would make that additive, but `identity.json`/`devices.json` have their own versioning (`IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION`), not `SCHEMA_VERSION`. [tree] to confirm whether a `devices.json` change needs a migration step.
- **No tombstone for a revoked device.** A revoked token and a never-known token are the same thing to the host: `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) answers 401 `unauthorized`, "the token is not known; pair again". The acceptance line "revoke the phone and the page says so on its next request" cannot be met from the current reply. It would need either a tombstone (hash of revoked tokens, a new durable record) or the page saying "not paired or revoked" for both. The issue asks for "revoked" and "identity changed" to be said plainly, so this is a decision.
- **The page's own state (client side), rehydrated per load:** the token (a cookie or `localStorage`, decision 2), the pinned `spki_sha256` and `server_id` from the pairing URL, the last revision. Everything else (sessions, conversation, screen) is in memory and refetched, as the Swift client does (§7 "What the client keeps": nothing from a host on disk). Rehydration of a page = load HTML, read the stored credential, `GET /api/v1/info`, open `/api/v1/events`, wait for `hello`, fetch snapshots, apply buffered events by revision (§4.4 "Subscribe first, then snapshot"). The existing protocol already gives that; the page re-implements the Swift client's reconcile (per-key held revision, epoch change refetches everything, `resync_required` reconnects).
- **The pairing window** is not saved (`PairingWindow` in core, `OpenPairing` at `src/core/remote.rs:46`; code made by `remote::pairing_code()`, 40 bits, single use, three failures close it). A URL carrying the code is therefore valid only while that in-memory window is open.
- **Host-side secrets:** key in Keychain as `remote-key:<server_id>`; token never stored, only its SHA-256. A web token in a cookie does not change this, but "keep tokens out of logs, URLs" (§5 line 318) now meets a request line that contains the code (see 3.4).

## 2. What exists, with files and lines

### The port (adapter): `src/adapters/remote.rs`
- `RemoteRequest` `:360` carries method, path (query stripped), query pairs, body, `bearer`, `upgrade`. There is **no cookie, no Origin, no Host, no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, no User-Agent field**. Only `authorization`, `upgrade`, `sec-websocket-key`, `content-length` are read in `read_request` (`:444`, bearer at `:487`, upgrade at `:491`); every other header is dropped. The user-agent for a device name (issue item 6) would be a new field.
- `RemoteReply` `:389` is `{status, body, authenticated}`: **no content type, no extra headers**. `respond` (`:530`) hardcodes `Content-Type: application/json` and `Connection: keep-alive`, with a status table that has no 304 and no 308. There is no `Set-Cookie`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Cache-Control` or `X-Content-Type-Options` anywhere (grep found none). `RemoteReply { .. }` is built by struct literal in about 28 places in `src/app.rs` (count from grep) plus the adapter, so adding a field is a mechanical but wide edit, unless a constructor or `Default` is added first.
- `respond_upgrade` (`:519`) writes a 101 with no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`. A browser that offered a subprotocol and gets none back fails the connection (see Open questions), so the subprotocol candidate needs a change here as well as in `read_request`.
- `connection` (`:770`): TLS handshake with 5 s (`HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT :570`), then a request/reply loop; first request within 5 s then `IDLE_TIMEOUT` 30 s (`:573`). `Limits::limited` (`:631`) rate-limits **only** `/api/v1/pair` (6/min) and `/api/v1/info` (60/min), per listener, not per client address. Every request, including any new static path, goes through `shared.requests.try_send` to the frame (inbox 64, drain 8 per pass) unless the adapter is changed to answer static files itself before that hand-off, as it already answers 429 and 503.
- Pools: a connection starts in the unauthenticated pool (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED = 4`, `:567`) and moves to the paired pool (12) only on a reply with `authenticated: true` (`:835`). The accept loop closes a fifth stranger at once (accept thread in `bind`, `:660`-ish). A static page reply would be `authenticated: false` (nothing paired about it), so a browser's page, CSS and JS loads, each possibly on parallel TLS connections, all sit in the 4-slot pool.
- Subscriber (`:878`): WebSocket fed from a queue of 256; a revoked device's queue is dropped (`dispatch_inner`, `src/app.rs:486`) and the socket closes.
- `make_identity` (`:95`): `CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())` means **no subject alternative names**, CN `Switchboard <server_id>`, key P-256, not_after year 4096. A browser sees a no-SAN, self-signed certificate on an IP-literal host.
- `local_address()` `:962` returns one IPv4 the system routes outward on, or `None`. No hostname, no `.local` name, no IPv6.

### The frame: `src/app.rs`
- `serve_remote` `:3017`. The first line is the allowlist's front door: `request.path.strip_prefix("/api/v1/")`, else a 404 `not_found` (`:3023`). `GET /` today is a 404. `info` and `pair` are served before `authenticate`; everything else needs the bearer.
- `authenticate` `:3127` reads `request.bearer` only. A cookie path means a second source of the token here, and the same function runs `DeviceSeen`.
- `remote_info` `:3568` (what `/info` says: server_id, server_name, protocol, capabilities, `spki_sha256`, version, limits, `pairing_open`). `remote_pair` `:3606` (checks window, then `spki_sha256` equals the host's own key, then code; makes the token; reply `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}`; `device_name` from body, default "Device"). The token travels in the JSON body, so a cookie needs a `Set-Cookie` on this one reply (decision 2).
- `remote_subscribe` `:2723` (requires `request.upgrade`, sends `hello`, registers `Subscriber{device}`); `?scope=all` includes Dispatch workers, plain does not (`hide_workers` `:2687`).
- `bind_remote` `:2936`: `0.0.0.0` when `identity.listen.lan`, else `127.0.0.1` (`:2963`). Bonjour advertises only on LAN.
- The 401 path: `refuse` `:3754` logs method, path and code only; the query is not logged (the path has the query stripped). So the code in `?code=` does not reach the log through `refuse`. [tree] a read of every `log::` that prints a request (none found for the query) would confirm.

### The pairing window UI: `src/ui/remote.rs`
- `pairing` `:141`. The QR payload is built at `:160` as JSON `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses: ["ip:port"]}`, rendered by `qr_texture` (`:172`), and the same string is what "Copy invite" (`:201`) copies. Text beside the QR: spaced code, short key (`short_hash`), address, scope. `window.scope` is chosen in the dialog (radio at the not-open branch) before the window opens; the browser inherits it through `new_device` (`src/core/remote.rs`, `PairedDevice.scope = pairing.scope`).
- The address is `local_address()` + `cx.remote_port` (`src/ui/mod.rs:401, 420`), i.e. a bare IPv4 and the bound port. If `local_address()` is `None` the payload's `addresses` is empty, and a URL has nothing to be a URL of.
- Devices grid `:229`: name, scope combo, "paired", "seen", Revoke. The dialog states redaction's limits in a sentence; the issue also wants the trust step stated there (decision 1).
- UI test that pins the invite format: `tests/ui.rs:7474` clicks "Copy invite" and parses the clipboard as JSON (`invite["code"]`, `invite["spki_sha256"]`). Changing the QR to a URL changes this test.
- Script: `src/script.rs:729` `pairing <code>|close`, `remote-devices`, `remote-listen lan|loopback <port>`; README lines ~276-280 document `switchboard-remote pair "$(pbpaste)"`.

### The native text path that must keep working
- `client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift:106-123`: `pair '<invite json>'` (one arg, `PairingInvite.parse`) or `pair <host:port> <code> <spki>`.
- `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:94-117`: `PairingInvite` is `Decodable` from JSON (`server_id`, `spki_sha256`, `code`, `addresses`), `parse` = `Wire.decode`. Other users: `client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:106` (a pasted line is tried as an invite) and `:883` (the pairing sheet), `ConnectionManager.swift:474,482`, `SwitchboardVisionApp.swift:56-61` (`SWITCHBOARD_INVITE`, invites' JSON), `client/scripts/sim.sh` (per design.md B1). A URL form means `PairingInvite.parse` accepts a URL (new parse branch plus fixtures/tests in `client/Tests/SwitchboardClientCoreTests/PairingTests.swift`), or the JSON stays and the URL is a second string.
- The URL has no `addresses` list, only the host it was opened at; the JSON carries `addresses` (an array). `id`, `key`, `code` map to `server_id`, `spki_sha256`, `code`.
- The Swift tests are not in the pre-commit hook or CI (design.md A2 status), so a Swift change here is checked only by hand.

### Wire/read models the page would use (`control/src/lib.rs`, `docs/remote-client.md` §4.3)
- `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637`) has: id, project, name, kind, cwd, notes, liveness, `card` (the card's word), last_exit, `last_stop_at_ms`, `quiet_secs`, `last_activity_ms`, `waiting`, `waiting_reason`, `trust_question`, `prompt_refusal`, `resume_id`, `op`, `pending`, wakeup/held times. **No excerpt field.** `last_message`, which the spec says (§4.3, `session.last_response` bullet) is "a field of the session's metadata", does not exist in this tree (grep of `src`, `control`, and the Swift `Views.swift` finds none). The one-line excerpt the card shows is drawn on the Mac from the transcript or the pane's last line (`caption_of`, `src/app.rs:4105`, `refresh_captions` `:1093`) and is not on the wire. So "each with ... the one-line excerpt the card shows" has no source over the port today: either a new additive `SessionView` field (wire crate change, fingerprint churn, Swift fixtures, `client/Fixtures/*.json` regenerated with `SWITCHBOARD_WRITE_FIXTURES=1`), or one `last-response` fetch per listed session (N requests, watch-set cap 128), or no excerpt in the first cut. The issue says "no new read model unless the page cannot do without one"; this is that case, in question form.
- Grouping by project needs `GET /projects` then `GET /projects/{id}/sessions` per project (no single all-sessions endpoint). `GET /waiting` is one collection of `SessionView`s. The card's ordering rule is `CardState::rank` (waiting first) in `all_sessions_sorted` (`src/core/action.rs:3190`), not exposed as a rank on the wire; the client must reproduce it from `card`/`waiting` (the Swift `Views.swift:140-147` does this with a switch over the word).
- Session view for Claude Code = `GET .../last-response` (a projection of the conversation key, watched through `watch {conversation}`); anything else = `GET .../screen?lines=n` (refused for a not-running session; watched through `watch {screen}`). Events: `changed {session|sessions|waiting|conversation|screen}`; the page sends `watch`/`unwatch` text frames. Send = `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` with `{op, text}`, `control` scope, 16 KiB cap; `op` is the idempotency key; timeout is followed by `GET /ops/{op}`, never a blind resend (§4.5).
- `info.capabilities` lists `control`, so "hidden when the device lacks control" has a source; the device's own scope is **not** on any read endpoint: `/info` is unauthenticated and says what the host can do, not what this token may do. The `/pair` reply has `scope`, but a page restoring from a stored cookie gets no scope back. No endpoint answers "who am I / what scope". (If the token is HttpOnly the page cannot read its own scope from a stored value either.) The issue wants "the device's scope and host name in the header"; scope would need either the page storing it at pair time (stale after a dialog change, which the spec says takes effect on the next request) or a small new endpoint, or a field in a reply envelope. This is a gap, not an answer.

### Tests
- `tests/remote.rs`: harness `port()` (`:52`), `http` (`:245`, a hand-rolled rustls client with a pinned config, sends `Authorization: Bearer`, parses status and `Content-Length` only: it ignores every other response header and cannot read a `Set-Cookie`, a `Content-Type`, or a CSP), `call`/`get` (`:299/327`), the pairing tests (`:477`, `:582`, `:635`), revocation (`:658`), allowlist (`:682`), rate limit (`:1406`), stalled strangers (`:3226`), fixtures (`:1587`, `:1829`).
- `info_is_served_to_anyone_and_every_other_read_is_refused_unpaired` (`:426`) asserts `GET /other` is `404 not_found` (`:464`) and `info` carries no key material. A `/` that serves a page must leave `/other` 404 and the test still true; but any test that treats "a path outside /api/v1 is refused" as the rule changes.
- The issue's own test line (decision 5), "no UI test drives a browser": confirmed in this tree (tests/ui.rs is egui kittest only). The CLI's pairing flow in Swift uses the pinned `HostClient`; the Rust side has no `reqwest`-like client in `src/`, so "the host's own HTTP client as the CLI does" means the hand-rolled `http` helper in `tests/remote.rs` (there is `remote::pinned_client` in the adapter, `:168`) or the Swift one. [tree] whether a non-test Rust HTTP client exists beyond `pinned_client` is not checked; the CLI is Swift.

## 3. Findings that bear on the decisions

1. **What a self-signed click-through buys is narrower than the issue's framing, and the `key` check has nothing to compare against in the browser.** Page JS cannot read the TLS certificate or its SPKI. The only "key presented by `/info`" available to the page is the `spki_sha256` field of the `/info` JSON, which is whatever the answering server writes. A page served by the impostor serves its own page and its own `/info`. So the URL's `key` guards against reaching the wrong genuine Switchboard by address (a reused DHCP address, two Macs), not against an attacker. On the host side, `remote_pair` (`:3606`) already refuses a `/pair` whose body key is not the host's own, and the page would put the URL's key in that body: against a genuine host that is the only meaningful check; against an impostor the impostor decides. That is the same as the issue's own statement; the notes add that the comparison is page-side and unenforceable from the host's point of view.
2. **Cookies are not port-scoped.** A cookie set by `https://192.168.1.5:43187` is sent to every other port on that host, and a `__Host-` prefix constrains Domain/Path/Secure but not port. Two Switchboard instances on one machine (the dev aid `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT`, and tests use it) would share a cookie name unless it carries the server id. `SameSite=Strict` is about site, not origin, so another page on a different port of the same IP is same-site: CSRF on `POST /send` and cross-site-WebSocket-hijack protections need an explicit check (Origin or Host, or a custom request header), none of which exists, because the port has only ever had bearer headers, which a cross-origin page cannot attach. Moving to ambient credentials (a cookie) removes that property for the whole `/api/v1` surface, including the native clients' routes: the cookie is accepted at the same endpoints. This is the largest security consequence of decision 2 and should be named in the plan.
3. **The unauthenticated pool is 4 and a browser's page load is bursty.** HTML, CSS, JS, favicon, `/info`, each possibly on its own TLS connection (browsers open up to ~6 per host), all unauthenticated until a reply with `authenticated: true`. A page load by a stranger-or-owner can occupy the pool, and the pool does not distinguish a browser from a flood. Static replies are also not rate-limited. If the page is served on the frame, it competes with the 8-per-pass drain and the 64 inbox; if served on the connection thread, that skips the frame (and the rule "handlers are thin; no logic in the adapter") but needs a pool decision. A paired browser also holds a paired slot per WebSocket for as long as the tab lives, out of 12 shared with the headset and the CLI.
4. **The pairing code lands in the host's request line.** A URL `GET /?code=...` is read by `read_request` into `RemoteRequest.query` (`:496-505`), so the code crosses the TLS connection and sits in the frame's memory like any query. It is not logged by `refuse` (path only). Also: the browser's history entry exists until `replaceState` runs, a `Referer` carries the URL to any subresource that is not same-origin (there should be none under the CSP the issue asks for), and some browsers sync history or open links from a camera app in a different process before the page script runs. A fragment (`#code=`) never reaches the host or a Referer and `replaceState` still works on it; the issue chose the query string. Whether that is deliberate is a question, not a finding.
5. **The code is single use, the URL is a bearer of it.** Anyone who can see the QR for the five-minute window (a screen share, a photo of the dialog) has the code; the key in the QR does not authenticate the person, as today with the JSON QR. No change from the native flow, but the URL is now also in the phone's camera/Messages/clipboard apps. Equivalent to "Copy invite".
6. **Cert has no SAN.** Even with the click-through, some browsers apply extra rules to certificates they treat as untrusted (HSTS-like blocks, no "Proceed" on some versions for no-SAN, ATS-like policies on iOS WebKit for `WebSocket`/`fetch`). Whether a no-SAN, IP-literal, self-signed P-256 certificate can be click-through-accepted on iOS Safari and Android Chrome, and whether that acceptance extends to `wss://` and to `fetch` is what decides option A (click-through) versus option B (host offers its certificate). Not checked.
7. **The spec's sentences to amend** (the plan is told to amend the spec and the status section): `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1 (bounds: "a TLS handshake..."; the pools; add the page's place in them), §4.3 (add the static paths, which are outside the `/api/v1` allowlist and not in the table; "Everything else on the wire is refused before translation" holds for `/api/v1` only), §5 (line 306 "Require pairing before anything but /info and /pair"; line 309 the QR payload JSON, "scans or types both"; line 312 "It is sent only as a bearer header ... never in a URL", which a cookie contradicts; line 313 "The client stores the token and the pinned key hash in its Keychain"; line 317 "The client verifies the pin on every connection" which a browser cannot), and the design.md sections "Remote client (2026-10-12)" (A1 sentence on "everything else is refused by name", "the QR carrying the server id, key hash, code and address") and "Known gaps". README (Layout row for `web/`, `src/adapters/remote.rs`, `src/ui/remote.rs`, `tests/remote.rs`; dev aids; the `pbpaste` pairing line at ~276), CHANGELOG Unreleased line, and the dialog's text.
8. **Static assets and the layering rule.** The page files are data embedded with `include_str!` (no precedent for text assets in `src`, only `include_bytes!` for fonts and the icon in `src/main.rs:167`, `src/ui/theme.rs:203`). A `web/` directory at the repo root would also need `Cargo.toml` `include`/`exclude` and the bundle script checks (`scripts/bundle.sh`) [tree] not read. CLAUDE.md: `src/core` is deterministic and `src/ui` only draws; the page is neither, it is adapter data. Where the path table lives (adapter or `app.rs`) is a design call; `serve_remote` is where the allowlist lives today.
9. **Hard rules touched.** No keystroke injection: not relevant to the page's own JS. Never write into a project's `.claude/`/`.switchboard/`: not touched. Secret values: the page shows redacted text only; the page's CSP and storage choice are what keep a token out of script reach. No client names anywhere that reaches GitHub: nothing in this issue needs one. Attribution: CLAUDE.md forbids a `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with" line in commits and PR bodies, overriding the harness reminder; the plan's commit and PR steps should say so.

## 4. Build order the tree suggests (for a planner, not settled)
Spec amendment and spike for the browser-trust facts first (CLAUDE.md: "add a new spike directory for any new risky mechanism before building on it"; there is none for browsers: `spikes/22-remote-port` covers the native pin and the visionOS pinning delegate is "not run"). Then adapter (reply headers, static route, cookie or subprotocol, Origin check, pools), core/app (auth source, scope/identity endpoint, user-agent device name), the page, the QR/URL and the native parse, tests (`tests/remote.rs`, `tests/ui.rs:7474`, Swift `PairingTests`), docs. Core changes need a core test in `src/core/tests.rs`; `AppAction`/`Effect`/model changes are additive only.

# Spikes

Throwaway crates and scripts that answered the Spike 0 questions in
`docs/design.md` before any product code was written. Each directory has a
README with the commands run, their output, and a recommendation. They are
kept for reference and are not built by the main crate.

| Dir | Question | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `01-claude-resume` | Can Claude Code sessions be captured and resumed? | Yes: `--session-id <uuid>` at launch, `--resume <uuid>` later from any terminal. Transcripts pruned after 30 days unless `cleanupPeriodDays` is raised. |
| `02-process-host` | tmux or own PTYs? | tmux on a private server: sessions outlive the app, reattach works, ~3 ms round trip. PTY adapter kept as fallback and for tests. |
| `03-session-state` | How to know "waiting on you"? | Claude Code hooks (`PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`) via a tiny `switchboard-hook` binary and a Unix socket; OSC 777 text from the raw stream as the hook-free fallback. |
| `05-keychain` | Can secrets live in the Keychain without prompts? | Yes for a bundle signed with a stable identity and identifier: the item ACL is `identifier + certificate`, so rebuilds read silently. Ad-hoc builds prompt per rebuild. |
| `06-pane-size` | Why is the embedded pane wider than the widget? | `window-size manual` ignored the client; `latest` makes the window follow whichever client attached last. Re-applied on launch for servers that outlive the app. |
| `07-clone-session` | Can a session be cloned up to a chosen message? | Yes: copy the transcript prefix before the chosen prompt, substitute a fresh UUID for `sessionId`, save it `0600` beside the original; `--resume <new>` opens the truncated history and the original is untouched. |
| `08-promptbox-embed` | Can Prompt Box be the agent message box? | Yes: same egui 0.36, drawn into a bottom panel unchanged, a `Clipboard` adapter turns Send into a hand-off; needs an embedded mode, a sink port, and focus-scoped shortcuts in promptbox. |
| `09-popout` | Can a session live in a window of its own? | Yes: an immediate viewport drawn from the main frame holds the page, terminal, and side panel; its frame is saved to settings and restored. |
| `10-nunchuk-serial` | Can a nunchuk drive the working set over USB serial? | Yes: one line per button change or stick flick from the Feather, read on a thread that reconnects; round trip 2 to 9 ms. Firmware in `firmware/nunchuk`. |
| `11-gate-sandbox` | Can Dispatch's pipeline commands be confined to the ticket's tree on macOS? | Yes: `sandbox-exec` with `(allow default)`, writes denied except the tree, the attempt directory, the lane's caches and a base set; ~5 ms start-up; a refused write is `EPERM` and a tagged `deny(1)` line in the unified log. `setuid` programs and keychain creation fail inside it. |
| `12-hidden-frames` | Does the frame loop keep running while the window is occluded or minimized? | Not before the fix: with the app hidden, a control query timed out after 10 s and was answered at once on unhide. With the tick and `pump` in `App::logic`, hidden queries answer in 75 to 103 ms (eframe's 100 ms throttle for invisible windows). The sleep and wake cycle is not yet measured. |
| `13-dispatch-service` | Can a Dispatch service be a Switchboard service session, and how is its port read? | Yes: `$SHELL -lc 'exec "$@"' dispatch-service env PORT=<port> npm start` finds `npm`, answers (CRA in 27 s), and is gone with its port 200 ms after `kill-session`. A port is free only if `0.0.0.0`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` all bind: CRA listens on `*`, which a loopback bind does not see. |
| `14-env-exec` | Do a pane's record id and launch token reach a child, so `switchboard-env exec` can resolve its sets? | Yes for a shell grandchild of a tmux pane started with `-e`; the binary's path is covered by `tests/control.rs`. The `aws-vault` form and the no-prompt run under Dispatch's launch flags were not run and are left to the owner. |
| `15-paste-buffer` | Can a multi-line send be bracketed only for a pane that asked for it? | Yes: `load-buffer -` then `paste-buffer -p -r -d` frames the text in `ESC[200~` .. `ESC[201~` for a pane with `bracket_paste_flag` 1 and delivers it bare otherwise; `-r` keeps LF, `-d` leaves no buffer. CR passes through and tmux 3.7c shows ESC as a literal `^[`, so the sender turns CR into LF and removes ESC. `send-keys -H` passes the markers to every pane. Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
| `16-base-pipeline` | Can Dispatch find a merged pull request's merge commit and read the base's pipeline on it? | GitHub, yes: `mergeCommit` on `gh pr list` and `gh pr view`, and the commit's `check-runs` (a short hash works) show the base's run in progress and then finished. Bitbucket's reads were not run (the token could not be read in the run); the adapter follows the documented `merge_commit.hash`, commit `statuses` and pipeline `steps`, with a read by number when a list row lacks the commit; until they are run, a wait on a Bitbucket base pipeline is refused. |
| `18-tmux-argv` | Do `new-session -e` values show in a process listing, and can they reach tmux another way? | Yes, they did: the server keeps the argv of the client that started it. `tmux start-server \; source-file -` with the `new-session` line on stdin keeps every value and the pane command off any argv; cold and warm both work, errors still return, and double-quoted values with `\n` for line breaks round-trip (single quotes lose a line starting with `#`). Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
| `19-structured-ask` | Does a card's answer to a structured ask reach interactive Claude Code as the next user message, sent once, both at the prompt and when held until the turn's `Stop`? | Yes: `Owner answered "<question>": <answer>`, typed as one line, arrived as its own user message once in both cases; a held answer went out only after the `Stop`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.293 by the ignored gate test `a_structured_answer_arrives_as_the_next_prompt`. |
| `21-evidence-writes` | Which writes reach a stage's evidence directory, outside the agent's cwd, without a prompt? | The Write tool, under the attempt directory's `Edit(//<dir>/**)` rule. Bash `cp`, `mv` and `mkdir` ask, and `--add-dir` does not change that. A Playwright MCP screenshot is refused outside the server's roots unless it runs with `--allow-unrestricted-file-access`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.295 and `@playwright/mcp@0.0.82`. |
| `22-remote-port` | Can a pinned-TLS HTTP and WebSocket port run on std with every request answered by the frame thread, and what does it cost? | Yes: `rustls` + `rcgen` + `tungstenite` + `mdns-sd`, no Tokio; the frame's share is under 0.25 ms per pass, latency is one frame interval, the pools and the subscriber overflow hold under a stall and an unread socket, Bonjour is seen by `dns-sd`. A 146 MB transcript parses in 290 ms at 575 MB peak, so content work leaves the frame thread. ctime and inode see the file changes mtime and size miss. |
| `04-terminal-view` | Embedded terminal or hand-off? | Hand off agents to Ghostty (`open -na Ghostty --args ... -e cmd`, raise by title); embed `egui_term` for shells, commands, services. |

Findings are folded into `docs/design.md` under "Spike 0 results".

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured).
